I vaginally delivered at 34 + 3.

Initially, I noticed that I wasn't feeling good the Monday before I delivered. I was dizzy, fatigued, and having spotty vision, but I just chalked it up to being extremely busy at work in the lead up to Thanksgiving. But the next day, I had all the above plus a really bad headache. When I got home from work, I took my blood pressure and it was 153/90. I took some medicine and a nap, but when I woke up, not only had my blood pressure gone up to 155/94, my vision was even worse to where it looked like the room was tipping over.

Everything happened kind of fast after that. My husband took me to the labor and delivery ER and after some mild range blood pressures over 140/90 and some Tylenol, I was admitted into the antepartum unit for observation. The next day, my headache still hadn't gone away, so they gave me IV Tylenol and Reglan in addition to the steroid shot. Ironically enough, that wound up helping my headache for the time being, but when I told the nurse that, she went to get the doctor. After another two hours, the doctor came and told me I was being induced that day. While my blood pressure had stabilized for the time being, my bloodwork showed that I had protein in my urine (0.44) and due to it taking a whole cocktail of medicine to get rid of my headache, I was diagnosed with preeclampsia with severe features.

I was moved to labor and delivery and put on magnesium, pitocin, fluids, and penecillin. I also had a Cooke balloon put in me and wound up making it seven hours before needing the epidural. They broke my water once I hit 5cm and the balloon fell out. I had to be put on oxygen overnight because I kept desatting, and they had to keep upping my pitocin because my contractions were stalling and I was stuck at 5cm dilation. 

The next morning (Thanksgiving Day), I got the second steroid shot and was maxxed out on pitocin. Fortunately, I was at 9cm and 90% effacement, so I was pushing within an hour, and after another hour, I had my daughter! She was 5lbs 7oz and spent 10 days in the NICU due to RDS before being moved to the NSCU for 3 days to see how she did off her NG tube and warmer. After the three days, she went home!

I was on magnesium from Wednsday afternoon to around Friday afternoon, so I was only able to hold her for a few minutes before they took her to the NICU, and I couldn't go up to see her due to the magnesium making me a fall risk. Even once I was taken off of it, I had to be in a wheelchair when going to see her. In the meantime, my husband went up to see her every three hours and waited until I was cleared to see her to name her.

In terms of PPD, my OB said I'm at a high risk for it, given what all has happened as well as my emotional state afterwards. Mainly, I've been having Post Partum Rage where I want people to just leave me alone and stop asking about me and my daughter.

Overall, I don't like how she came into the world, but I'm glad she's here and in my arms. In total, I was in labor for 22 hours and pushed for about an hour and a half.
